memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"except for a close relative, such as his mother or father, his son or
daughter, his brother, or an unmarried sister who is dependent on him
since she has no husband - for her he may make himself unclean. He
must not make himself unclean for people related to him by marriage,
and so defile himself" - Lev 21:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is something beautiful hidden inside a law book. God does not
demand that His priests become emotionless. He makes space for their
sorrow. A father, a mother, a child, a brother, an unmarried sister
who had no one else to care for her - for these, the priest could
mourn in the ordinary human way.

God knew what grief does to a heart. He did not ask His servants to
pretend they felt nothing when their own family died. Holiness in
Scripture has never meant coldness.

Notice too the mention of the unmarried sister with no husband. In
that society she was among the most vulnerable. God specifically
protected her right to be mourned by her brother. Our God notices the
ones society tends to overlook.

Dear reader, if you are grieving today, hear this clearly: your tears
are not a failure of faith. Jesus Himself wept at a grave, even
knowing He was about to raise His friend (John 11:35). Paul does not
tell believers to stop grieving; he tells us not to grieve as those
without hope (1 Thess 4:13).

You may weep. You simply weep with a Saviour who has already defeated
the grave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I felt guilty for grieving, as though faith should remove
   sorrow?
2. Who in my circle is grieving and could use my quiet presence?
3. How does the resurrection change the way I face loss?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You understand tears and do not despise them.
Comfort those I know who are walking through loss, and hold my own
heart in hope. Amen.
